title: Boundary-value decay conjecture for Sierpinski gasket monomials
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $r>0$, let $P_{j,k}^{(r)}$ be the degree-$j$ monomial in the $k$th family associated with the $r$-dependent Laplacian, and let $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ denote the supremum norm. Let $\lambda_2(r)$ and $\lambda_3(r)$ be the relevant Neumann eigenvalues, and let $g(r)$ be the continuous function from the ratio-existence conjecture.

**Boundary-value decay conjecture.** For $r\neq 1$ and $r\neq\frac{\sqrt{17}-3}{4}$,

$$
\|P_{j,1}^{(r)}\|_\infty=O\left(|2\lambda_3(r)-\lambda_2(r)|^{-j}\right).
$$

For $r\neq\frac{\sqrt{17}-3}{4}$,

$$
\|P_{j,2}^{(r)}\|_\infty=O\left(|2\lambda_3(r)-\lambda_2(r)|^{-j}\right).
$$

For all but at most finitely many values of $r$,

$$
\|P_{j,3}^{(r)}\|_\infty=O\left(|g(r)|^j\right).
$$

These estimates would give growth restrictions on coefficients in Taylor series on the Sierpinski gasket and help determine convergence and rearrangement behavior. They are presented as consequences of the preceding conjectural ratio statements and are not established in the supplied text.
quantifiers_and_scope: For each positive r outside the respective exceptional sets, asymptotic j bounds for all three monomial families; the third permits finitely many r exceptions.
technical_assessment: Monomials, eigenvalue ordering and conjectural g are external definitions. Ratio limits alone do not imply uniform supremum-norm bounds at the asserted exact exponential rate. Reference reports refutation without identifying this precise clause; no retirement.

title: Generalized union property conjecture
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $n,k,s,q$ be integers with $n>q\ge k$, $sk>q$, and $s\ge2$. A $k$-graph ${\mathcal F}\subset {[n]\choose k}$ has property $U(s,q)$ if

$$
|F_1\cup\cdots\cup F_s|\le q
$$

for every choice of $F_1,\ldots,F_s\in{\mathcal F}$. Let $m(n,k,s,q)$ be the maximum of $|{\mathcal F}|$ over all $k$-graphs having property $U(s,q)$. For $p\ge r>0$, write ${\mathcal A}_{p,r}=\{A\in {[n]\choose k}:|A\cap[p]|\ge r\}$.

**Generalized union property conjecture.** For all choices of $n,k,s,q$, one has $m(n,k,s,q)=|{\mathcal A}_{p,r}|$ for an appropriate choice of $p,r>0$ such that ${\mathcal A}_{p,r}$ has property $U(s,q)$. More precisely, if

$$
q=(k-r)s+p\qquad\text{and}\qquad r\le p\le s+r-2,
$$

then

$$
m(n,k,s,q)=\max_{0\le i\le k-r}|{\mathcal A}_{p+is,r+i}|.
$$

This conjecture is intended to unify the Complete Intersection Theorem and the Erdős matching conjecture by treating restrictions on the union of several edges. Its general status is open.
quantifiers_and_scope: All integers n>q>=k, s>=2, sk>q, with the displayed p,r compatibility, exact extremal maximum.
technical_assessment: Contains matching and complete-intersection regimes; compression must select an extremizer from the entire shifted family, not merely verify proposed examples. No finite certificate proves all n,k,s,q; no general route.

title: The potential crossing pair characterization of graphs with crossing number at least 2
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $G$ be a non-planar graph. A pair of edges $\{e,f\}$ of $G$ is a **potential crossing pair** if, for every Kuratowski subgraph $H$ of $G$, $e$ and $f$ form a crossing pair of $H$. The crossing number of $G$, denoted by $\operatorname{cr}(G)$, is the minimum number of crossings in a drawing of $G$ in the plane.

**Potential crossing pair conjecture.** The graph $G$ has crossing number at least $2$ if and only if it does not have a potential crossing pair.

This question arises from the characterization of crossing pairs in the preceding theorem: a potential crossing pair that is not separated by cycles is a crossing pair. Thus, any potential crossing pair in a graph with crossing number at least $2$ would necessarily be separated by cycles. The source does not provide a resolution of this characterization.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every nonplanar graph: cr>=2 iff no edge pair crosses every Kuratowski subdivision.
technical_assessment: Crossing pair of a subdivision and separated-by-cycles convention need primary definitions. A pair meeting each obstruction does not by itself give one consistent plane drawing. The stated preceding theorem explicitly leaves this obstruction.

title: The full symmetric Galois group conjecture for rational plane curves
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $\mathbf{d}$ be a degree, let $P$ be a set of $3\mathbf{d}-1$ points of $\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{Q})$ in general position, let $C_P$ be the set of $N_{\mathbf{d}}$ complex rational plane curves of degree $\mathbf{d}$ through $P$, and let $L_P\subseteq\mathbb{C}$ be the splitting field of the Galois module $C_P$. Here $N_{\mathbf{d}}$ is the number of such curves. **Full symmetric Galois group conjecture.** For all $P$ outside a thin subset of $({\mathbb{P}}^2)^{3\mathbf{d}-1}(\mathbb{Q})$, we have

$$
\operatorname{Gal}(L_P/\mathbb{Q})=S_{N_{\mathbf{d}}}.
$$

The conjecture says that, for almost all configurations of rational points, the splitting field of the rational plane curves through them has the largest possible Galois group. The question is motivated by the study of the deck transformations of the generic fibre of the product of evaluation maps on the moduli space of maps to $\mathbb{P}^2$; the source does not state a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
quantifiers_and_scope: For every degree, outside a thin set of rational configurations, full symmetric action on all rational curves.
technical_assessment: General-position locus, multiplicities and moduli definitions need primary body. Generic monodromy plus arithmetic specialization would require substantial geometric dependencies; low-degree examples have no full-scope force.

title: Quantitative intrinsic connectivity conjecture for semilinear positive phases
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $f\in C_0^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ satisfy $f\ge0$ and $f(s)=0$ for all $s\le0$. Let $u$ solve

$$
\Delta u=f(u)\quad\text{in }\mathbb{R}^3,
$$

and suppose that the blow-down limit

$$
U(x)=\lim_{\epsilon\to0^+}\epsilon\,u(x/\epsilon)
$$

exists and has connected positive phase $\{x\in\mathbb{R}^3:U(x)>0\}$. **Quantitative intrinsic connectivity conjecture.** The minimum path distance between points in $\{x\in\mathbb{R}^3:u(x)>0\}$ is comparable to their Euclidean straight-line distance, with a comparison constant depending only on $U$, or perhaps even an absolute constant.

The conjecture asserts that connectedness of the blow-down positive phase prevents arbitrarily thin or long intrinsic bottlenecks in the positive phase of $u$. The source presents the universal-constant formulation as a possible strengthening, and gives no evidence of resolution.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every allowed f and entire solution with connected blow-down phase; one metric comparison constant depending only on U, possibly universal.
technical_assessment: No solution class, mode of blow-down convergence or precise uniformity is given. Connectivity alone supplies no quantitative bottleneck bound; elementary path connectivity does not establish a uniform intrinsic metric estimate.

title: The mod-9 partition conjectures
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $n=\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\cdots+\lambda_k$ be a partition written in weakly increasing order. Say that it satisfies **Condition($i$)** if

$$
\lambda_{j+2}-\lambda_j\geq 3\quad (1\leq j\leq k-2)
$$

and, whenever $\lambda_{j+1}-\lambda_j\leq 1$,

$$
\lambda_{j+1}+\lambda_j\equiv i\pmod 3\quad (1\leq j\leq k-1).
$$

For all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, the following five pairs of partition families are equinumerous: (1) partitions satisfying Condition($0$), and partitions whose parts are congruent to $\pm1$ or $\pm3$ modulo $9$; (2) partitions satisfying Condition($0$) with smallest part at least $2$, and partitions whose parts are congruent to $\pm2$ or $\pm3$ modulo $9$; (3) partitions satisfying Condition($0$) with smallest part at least $3$, and partitions whose parts are congruent to $\pm3$ or $\pm4$ modulo $9$; (4) partitions satisfying Condition($2$) with smallest part at least $2$, and partitions whose parts are congruent to $2$, $3$, $5$, or $8$ modulo $9$; (5) partitions satisfying Condition($1$) without an appearance of $2+2$ as a sub-partition, and partitions whose parts are congruent to $1$, $4$, $6$, or $7$ modulo $9$.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every integer n, five exact partition-count equalities.
technical_assessment: Finite coefficient tests only validate instances. A full route needs five generating-series identities or bijections respecting distance-two and adjacent congruence restrictions; no such new mechanism established. Known-identity/prior-body gate remains open.

title: Multiplicity stability conjecture for $VIC(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})$-modules
statement_exact_utf8: For a prime $p$ and a positive integer $k$, consider the irreducible complex representations of $GL_n(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})$ for all $n$, together with a compatible collection of labelings. A finitely generated $VIC(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})$-module is a functor with finite generation under the morphisms of $VIC(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})$. **Multiplicity stability conjecture.** For every $p,k$ there exists a compatible collection of labelings of the irreducible complex representations of $GL_n(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})$ for all $n$ such that finitely generated $VIC(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})$-modules exhibit multiplicity stability with respect to this labeling. This would extend the known multiplicity-stability phenomenon for $VIC(\mathbb{F}_p)$-modules, but the source notes that suitable labelings for the higher prime-power groups are not known.
quantifiers_and_scope: For every prime p and exponent k there exists one compatible labeling giving stability for every finitely generated VIC module.
technical_assessment: Compatible labeling and multiplicity stability not defined sufficiently in record. Choosing stable names after seeing a module would reverse quantifiers. Higher prime-power representation classification is not a small certificate.

title: List decodability of Reed-Solomon codes up to capacity
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field and let $D\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q$ be an evaluation set. For rate $\rho>0$, write $\mathsf{RS}[\mathbb{F}_q,D,\rho]$ for the corresponding Reed-Solomon code, and let ${\mathcal L}(\mathbb{F}_q,D,d,\delta)$ denote the maximum, over received words, of the number of codewords within relative Hamming distance $\delta$, where $d=\rho|D|$.

**List decodability of Reed-Solomon codes up to capacity.** For every $\rho>0$, there is a constant $C_\rho$ such that every Reed-Solomon code of length $n$ and rate $\rho$ is list-decodable from a $1-\rho-\varepsilon$ fraction of errors with list size at most $\left(\frac{n}{\varepsilon}\right)^{C_\rho}$. Equivalently,

$$
{\mathcal L}(\mathbb{F}_q,D,d=\rho|D|,1-\rho-\varepsilon)\leq\left(\frac{|D|}{\varepsilon}\right)^{C_\rho}.
$$

This conjecture proposes list decodability up to the information-theoretic capacity threshold, with polynomial list size in the block length and inverse gap parameter. The surrounding discussion notes that it is consistent with known limitations and contrasts it with the weaker Johnson-bound guarantee; its resolution status is not specified in the source.
quantifiers_and_scope: For each rate rho one exponent controls every field and evaluation set and every admissible epsilon.
technical_assessment: Random/punctured evaluation-set capacity results would not establish every-code claim. Worst-case received words and field sizes prevent promotion from generic-code constructions; no uniform polynomial bound route.

title: Commutator-vanishing conjecture for homogeneous conjugacy-invariant pseudo-lengths
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $\langle \alpha, \beta \rangle=\langle \alpha,\beta\rangle$ be the free group on two generators. A **homogeneous, conjugacy-invariant pseudo-length function** $l$ on $\langle \alpha, \beta \rangle$ is assumed to satisfy the corresponding homogeneity, conjugacy-invariance, and pseudo-length axioms. **Commutator-vanishing conjecture.** For every such function $l$,

$$
l(\alpha\beta\alpha^{-1}\beta^{-1})=0.
$$

This conjecture arose from attempts to construct a positive homogeneous, conjugacy-invariant length on the free group. The paper explains that the subsequent results of the polymath project show, in a strong sense, that homogeneous conjugacy-invariant length functions occur only on abelian groups and arise as restrictions of norms on subgroups of vector spaces; thus the conjecture is resolved by those results.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every homogeneous conjugacy-invariant pseudo-length on the free group kills its commutator.
technical_assessment: Primary arXiv1904.05214v1 Definitions1.1-1.3, Conjecture2.1, Lemma2.3 and Theorem2.4 read. Theorem2.4 states exact conclusion; surrounding random-walk argument explains O(sqrt(n))/n. Source contains a sign/transcription issue in homogeneity for negative exponents; conventional nonnegative/absolute homogeneity intended. Already public, zero credit; cited original full dependency body not replayed.

title: The multi-hypergraph Berge-tree Turán conjecture
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $n,k,r$ be positive integers, let $T$ be a $k$-edge tree, and let $\operatorname{ex}_r^{multi}(n,\mathcal{B}T)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $r$-uniform multi-hypergraph on $n$ vertices containing no Berge copy of $T$. The theorem preceding the conjecture proves the bound for $r\geq (k-1)(k-2)$.

**Multi-hypergraph Berge-tree Turán conjecture.** For all $r\geq k+1$,

$$
\operatorname{ex}_r^{multi}(n,\mathcal{B}T)\leq \frac{n(k-1)}{r}.
$$

For every non-star tree $T$, equality should hold if and only if $r$ divides $n$ and the extremal multi-hypergraph is $\frac{n}{r}$ disjoint hyperedges, each with multiplicity $k-1$. This conjecture extends the preceding theorem to the wider range $r\geq k+1$; the supplied text gives no resolution beyond the theorem's established parameter range.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every k-edge tree and r>=k+1, all n; nonstar equality characterization.
technical_assessment: Existing stated theorem for r>=(k-1)(k-2) covers only a parameter range. Repeated edges complicate leaf deletion and equality; proving one tree or one r gives no full outcome. No general charging invariant established.

title: Extremum-count conjecture for average normalized Penrose–Banzhaf power indices
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $\Delta_n$ be the probability simplex, equipped with the uniform distribution, and let ${\Greekmath 010C}_k^{\downarrow}$ denote the normalized Penrose–Banzhaf power index of the $k$-th largest player in a weighted voting game with quota $q$. Write $\mathbb{E}({\Greekmath 010C}_k^{\downarrow})$ for its average over the simplex.

**Extremum-count conjecture.** For every $k=1,\ldots,n$, the function $q\mapsto\mathbb{E}({\Greekmath 010C}_k^{\downarrow})$ has exactly $k-1$ local extrema on $(1/2,1)$.

This conjecture describes the regularity suggested by the paper’s Monte Carlo experiments: the largest player’s average power is monotone, while successive players exhibit increasing numbers of extrema. The statement is supported there only by numerical observation, and no proof or resolution is supplied.
quantifiers_and_scope: For each n and rank k=1..n, exactly k-1 local extrema on the open quota interval.
technical_assessment: Normalized-index zero denominators, quota tie rules and strict versus nonstrict local extrema need body. Piecewise-rational averages over simplex chambers are possible bounded computations but no general n extremum count follows; tiny-n endpoint quirks earn no credit.

title: Extremal triangle-count conjecture for bounded book number
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $b(G)$ be its book number. For nonnegative integers $b$ and $n$ with $b\leq n/4$, let $S_{b,n}$ be the graph obtained by blowing up the $3$-prism so that four parts have size $b$ and the other two have sizes $\lfloor(n-4b)/2\rfloor$ and $\lceil(n-4b)/2\rceil$. Thus $S_{b,n}$ has $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ edges, book number $b$ when $b\geq n/6$, and $b^2(n-4b)$ triangles. **Extremal triangle-count conjecture.** If $n/6\leq b<n/4$, then every graph on $n$ vertices with at least $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ edges and book number at most $b$, other than the balanced complete bipartite graph, has at least

$$
b^2(n-4b)
$$

triangles, with equality if and only if the graph is $S_{b,n}$. This conjecture predicts the exact minimum triangle count in the stated range and is confirmed in the source for $b/n=1/6$ and for $0.2495\leq b/n<1/4$.
quantifiers_and_scope: For n/6<=b<n/4, all n-vertex graphs at the edge threshold with book<=b excluding balanced bipartite; exact triangle bound and unique equality.
technical_assessment: Checking prism blow-ups is an upper construction, not the universal lower bound. Supplied endpoint and near-quarter results leave an interval; no short reduction closes it or proves rigidity.

title: Constrained minimum output entropy conjecture for Gaussian quantum-limited amplifiers
statement_exact_utf8:
For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\rho$ be an $n$-mode quantum state and define

$$
\omega_{\rho}=\left[\omega\left(g^{-1}\left(\tfrac{1}{n}S(\rho)\right)\right)\right]^{\otimes n},
$$

where $\omega_{\rho}$ is the $n$-mode thermal quantum Gaussian state with the same entropy as $\rho$. Let $\mathcal{A}_{\kappa}^{\otimes n}$ be the $n$-mode Gaussian quantum-limited amplifier with $\kappa\ge1$.

**Constrained minimum output entropy conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\rho$ and $\kappa\ge1$,

$$
S\left(\mathcal{A}_{\kappa}^{\otimes n}(\rho)\right)\ge S\left(\mathcal{A}_{\kappa}^{\otimes n}(\omega_{\rho})\right)=n\,g\left(\kappa g^{-1}\left(\tfrac{1}{n}S(\rho)\right)+\kappa-1\right).
$$

Thermal Gaussian inputs are known to minimize the output entropy in the one-mode case, while the general $n\ge2$ conjecture remains open except for entanglement-breaking Gaussian channels.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every number of modes n, every state rho and amplifier gain>=1, at fixed entropy.
technical_assessment: Thermal state, entropy domain and Gaussian channel need source definitions. Single-mode minimization cannot be tensorized over entangled inputs by independent scalar optimization; no full quantum entropy route.

title: Pach–Tardos conjecture for ordered uniform forests
statement_exact_utf8:
An **ordered $r$-uniform forest** is an $r$-uniform hypergraph whose vertex set is linearly ordered and whose edges admit an ordering $e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_t$ such that, for every $i\in\{2,3,\ldots,t\}$, there is an $h<i$ with

$$
e_i\cap\bigcup_{j<i}e_j\subseteq e_h.
$$

The **interval chromatic number** of an ordered hypergraph is the least number of consecutive intervals in the vertex ordering whose union gives a proper coloring. Let ${\rm ex}_{\rightarrow}(n,F)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex ordered $r$-uniform hypergraph containing no ordered copy of $F$.

**Pach–Tardos conjecture for ordered forests.** Let $r\geq 2$. Then for any ordered $r$-uniform forest $F$ with interval chromatic number $r$,

$$
{\rm ex}_{\rightarrow}(n,F)=O\bigl(n^{r-1}\cdot\operatorname{polylog} n\bigr).
$$

This extends the graph conjecture of Pach and Tardos to uniform hypergraphs. The source notes that the corresponding polynomial bound without the polylogarithmic factor is elementary for $r$-uniform forests, but gives no resolution of the strengthened conjecture.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every r>=2 and ordered r-uniform forest of interval chromatic number r; asymptotic all n with F-dependent polylog factors.
technical_assessment: Discarding vertex order loses exactly the hard obstruction. Ordinary forest extremal bounds do not give the ordered polylogarithmic estimate. No bounded certificate for arbitrary ordered patterns.

title: Lovász–Simonovits conjecture on the Erdős–Rademacher problem
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $K_r$ denote the complete graph on $r$ vertices. For integers $n$ and $m$ with $0\leq m\leq {n\choose 2}$, let $G_r(n,m)$ be the minimum number of copies of $K_r$ in an $(n,m)$-graph, meaning a graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. Let $\mathcal{H}$ consist of all graphs obtained from a complete multipartite graph by adding a triangle-free graph into one of its parts, and let $H_r(n,m)$ be the minimum number of $r$-cliques in an $(n,m)$-graph from $\mathcal{H}$. **Lovász–Simonovits conjecture.** For every integer $r\geq 3$, there is $n_0$ such that for all $n\geq n_0$ and $0\leq m\leq {n\choose 2}$, we have

$$
G_r(n,m)\geq H_r(n,m).
$$

Since every graph in $\mathcal{H}$ is an admissible $(n,m)$-graph, the reverse inequality $G_r(n,m)\leq H_r(n,m)$ is immediate; thus the conjecture asserts equality for sufficiently large $n$. It is a central open problem in the Erdős–Rademacher problem concerning the minimum number of cliques forced by a given number of edges.
quantifiers_and_scope: For each r>=3 exists n0; every n>=n0 and feasible edge count, exact minimum achieved in H.
technical_assessment: Asymptotic clique density alone does not imply exact finite extremizers across all m. The reverse inequality is trivial and earns no credit; no stability-to-exactness route supplied.

title: Prefix palindromic length conjecture for non-ultimately periodic words
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $u=u[1]u[2]\cdots$ be an infinite word. For $n\in\mathbb N$, let $PPL_u(n)$ denote the minimum number of concatenated palindromes needed to express the prefix of $u$ of length $n$. Let $SP_u(k)$ denote the length of the shortest prefix of $u$ having palindromic length $k$, with $SP_u(k)=\infty$ if no such prefix exists. **Prefix palindromic length conjecture.** For every non-ultimately periodic word $u$, the function $PPL_u(n)$ is unbounded, equivalently,

$$
SP_u(k)<\infty\quad\text{for every }k\in\mathbb N.
$$

The conjecture was formulated by the author with Puzynina and Zamboni; it is known for $p$-power-free words and more generally for words satisfying a $(p,l)$-condition, and it has also been proved for all Sturmian words. It remains unresolved for some non-ultimately periodic words.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every nonultimately periodic infinite word has unbounded prefix palindromic length.
technical_assessment: Power-free or Sturmian subclasses omit arbitrary recurrent powers. A finite prefix never certifies all infinite extensions; no full combinatorial periodicity mechanism established.

title: Jena–Genin–Mosca conjecture on single-qudit Clifford partitioning
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $q$ be prime, let $\mathcal{S}\subseteq \pauli{q}[*]$ be a set of generalized Pauli operators, let $sq\mathcal{C}$ denote the gate set of single-qudit Clifford operators, and let $m$ be the length of the largest Pauli operator in $\mathcal{S}$. A partition is a collection of parts whose operators are simultaneously diagonalizable by elements of the specified gate set. **Jena–Genin–Mosca conjecture.** Given $\mathcal{S}\subseteq \pauli{q}[*]$, the number of parts in a minimal partition of $\mathcal{S}$ with respect to $sq\mathcal{C}$ is expected to be bounded below by

$$
\left( \frac{1}{2} + o(1) \right) m(\log_2(q) - o(1)) \frac{|\mathcal{S}|}{\log_2(|\mathcal{S}|)}.
$$

The bound expresses the expected cost of restricting measurements to single-qudit Clifford operations, compared with arbitrary Clifford operations. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
quantifiers_and_scope: Claimed asymptotic lower bound in m,q,|S| on minimal single-qudit-Clifford measurement parts.
technical_assessment: Expected versus worst-case quantifier and o(1) regimes unspecified; the Pauli macro is unresolved. Large commuting product sets threaten a literal universal reading but that is a wording issue until actual primary passage is checked.

title: The parity-condition conjecture for large acyclic fillings
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $K_n^d$ be the full $d$-dimensional simplicial complex on $n$ vertices. For a non-trivial $(d-1)$-cycle $Z^{d-1}$, a **$0$-deficit filling** is an acyclic filling whose support has the largest possible size. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$, the **parity condition** is the requirement that, when $d$ is even,

$$
|Z^{d-1}| \equiv {{n-1} \choose d} \pmod{2}.
$$

**Large-filling conjecture.** Over $\mathbb{F}_2$, for every $d\geq 0$ there exists a number $n_d$ such that every non-trivial $(d-1)$-cycle $Z^{d-1}$ on $K_n^d$, with $n\geq n_d$, has a $0$-deficit filling if and only if the parity condition holds. Moreover, regardless of the parity condition, every non-trivial $(d-1)$-cycle has an acyclic filling of deficit $1$. Over $\mathbb{Q}$, for sufficiently large $n$, every $(d-1)$-cycle $Z^{d-1}$ has a $0$-deficit filling.

The parity condition is an obstruction over $\mathbb{F}_2$ for even $d$, since the parity of the filling's support must agree with that of its boundary. The conjecture predicts that this is the only obstruction to $0$-deficit fillings over $\mathbb{F}_2$ for sufficiently large complexes, while over $\mathbb{Q}$ no such obstruction remains; the source provides no resolution status.
quantifiers_and_scope: For each dimension eventually all nontrivial cycles over F2/Q; parity criterion for zero deficit, plus deficit-one existence.
technical_assessment: Acyclic support, coefficient field, meaning of exact deficit1 versus at-most1 and d=0 conventions require source. Inductive cones can accumulate dimension-dependent errors; no full parity-sufficient construction established.

title: The bounded-deficit conjecture for the FILL procedure
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $K_n^d$ be the full $d$-dimensional simplicial complex on $n$ vertices, and let $Z^{d-1}$ be a non-trivial $(d-1)$-cycle with coefficients in either $\mathbb{F}_2$ or $\mathbb{Q}$. Let $\operatorname{FILL}(Z_n^{d-1})$ denote the recursive filling procedure used in the source, and let the **deficit** of a filling measure how far its support is from the largest possible support.

**Bounded-deficit conjecture.** There exists a function $\alpha:\mathbb{N}\mapsto\mathbb{N}$, with $d\mapsto\alpha_d$, such that for every non-trivial $(d-1)$-cycle $Z^{d-1}$ on $K_n^d$, with coefficients in either $\mathbb{F}_2$ or $\mathbb{Q}$, the procedure $\operatorname{FILL}(Z_n^{d-1})$ can be made to produce a filling of deficit at most $\alpha_d$.

This is presented as a weaker conjecture than the paper's main conjecture: it predicts a deficit bounded independently of $n$, although the bound may depend on $d$. The source gives no resolution status.
quantifiers_and_scope: Exists alpha(d) independent of n and cycle, attainable by choices in FILL over either field.
technical_assessment: FILL choices and deficit are not specified. Arbitrary chain solving is not the named recursive procedure. A recurrence growing with n does not prove bounded deficit; no verified invariant.

title: Li et al.'s Tutte-path conjecture for rank-three hypergraph line graphs
statement_exact_utf8:
A **hypergraph** is a collection of subsets, called edges, of a ground set; its **rank** is the maximum edge size. Its line graph has one vertex for each hypergraph edge, with adjacency when two hypergraph edges intersect. A **Tutte path** is an $(a,b)$-path whose off-path components have at most three neighbours on the path, and a path is **maximal** if it cannot be extended while preserving the relevant path conditions.

**Li et al.'s conjecture.** For every pair of vertices $a,b$ of a connected line graph of a hypergraph of rank at most $3$, there is a maximal $(a,b)$-path which is a Tutte path.

The source presents this as an equivalent formulation of Thomassen's open conjecture. It is consequently open, although it is known to be equivalent to the line-graph Hamilton-cycle formulation.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every connected rank<=3 hypergraph line graph and every endpoint pair admits the asserted maximal Tutte path.
technical_assessment: Maximal relevant-path conditions need source. Record identifies equivalent Thomassen problem, so solving low rank examples or finding one path is not a full route. Off-path attachments remain global obstruction.

title: Schalekamp–Williamson–van Zuylen conjecture on the subtour-LP integrality gap
statement_exact_utf8: Consider the metric traveling salesperson problem and its subtour linear programming relaxation. A feasible solution is **half-integral** if every edge variable satisfies $x_e\in\{0,1/2,1\}$. The integrality gap is the supremum, over instances, of the ratio between the cost of an optimal tour and the cost of an optimal subtour-LP solution. **Schalekamp–Williamson–van Zuylen conjecture.** The integrality gap for the subtour LP is attained on half-integral vertices of the polytope. Equivalently, half-integral LP solutions have the largest integrality gap among all fractional solutions. This conjecture identifies half-integral instances as the hardest instances for metric TSP. The paper's $1.49993$-approximation algorithm for half-integral solutions would imply the same upper bound for the subtour-LP integrality gap if the conjecture holds.
quantifiers_and_scope: Supremal metric-TSP subtour gap may be restricted to half-integral vertices over all instance sizes.
technical_assessment: Attained versus supremum and vertices versus arbitrary feasible half-integral points are conflated. Rounding special half-integral solutions does not transfer arbitrary LP vertices to this class; no gap-preserving map.

title: Almost simple groups polynomial bound conjecture
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $X$ be a finite almost simple group, meaning that its socle $\operatorname{soc} X$ is a nonabelian simple group and $\operatorname{soc} X\leq X\leq \operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{soc} X)$. For a normal subgroup $N$ of a finite group $G$, define

$$
m(G,N):=m(G)-m(G/N),
$$

where $m(G)$ is the largest size of a minimal generating set. Let $\pi(S)$ denote the set of prime divisors of $|S|$. **Almost simple groups polynomial bound conjecture.** There exist constants $\sigma$ and $\eta$ such that, for every finite almost simple group $X$,

$$
m(X,\operatorname{soc} X)\leq \sigma\cdot |\pi(\operatorname{soc} X)|^\eta.
$$

The paper presents this as the almost-simple reduction of the polynomial bound conjecture; it is known for alternating and sporadic socles, while the Lie-type case remains substantially open.
quantifiers_and_scope: Universal sigma,eta bound m(X,soc X) polynomially in number of prime divisors for all finite almost-simple X.
technical_assessment: Alternating/sporadic families alone omit Lie type. Need simultaneous group-generation and arithmetic control across ranks and fields; no small universal witness or uniform route.

title: Equitable Vertex Arboricity Conjecture for bounded-degree graphs
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree at most $\Delta$. An **equitable tree-$k$-coloring** of $G$ assigns each vertex a color in $\{1,2,\ldots,k\}$ so that every color class induces a forest and the sizes of any two color classes differ by at most $1$. The equitable vertex arborable threshold $va_{eq}^*(G)$ is the least integer $k$ such that $G$ has an equitable tree-$k'$-coloring for every integer $k'\geq k$.

**Equitable Vertex Arboricity Conjecture.** Every graph with maximum degree at most $\Delta$ is equitably tree-$k$-colorable for every integer $k\geq (\Delta+1)/2$; equivalently,

$$
va_{eq}^*(G)\leq \lceil(\Delta+1)/2\rceil.
$$

Wu, Zhang and Li proposed this conjecture. It is known for all 5-degenerate graphs, and hence for graphs with maximum degree at most $5$, but remains open in general.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every graph max degree<=Delta and every integer k>=ceil((Delta+1)/2) admits equitable induced-forest coloring.
technical_assessment: Greedy proper coloring loses the factor two; acyclic recoloring must also preserve balance for every larger k. Low-degree instances do not cover general Delta; no full recoloring invariant.

title: Habegger–Pila optimal-subvariety conjecture for abelian varieties
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field and let $d$ be a non-negative integer. Let $A$ be an abelian variety defined over $K$ and let $V$ be a subvariety of $A$. For a subvariety $U$ of $A$, let $\langle U\rangle$ be the smallest special subvariety containing it and define its defect by

$$
\delta(U)=\dim\langle U\rangle-\dim U.
$$

A subvariety $W$ of $V$ is **optimal** for $V$ in $A$ if $\delta(U)>\delta(W)$ for every subvariety $U$ with $W\subsetneq U\subset V$.

**Habegger–Pila optimality conjecture.** The subvariety $V$ contains at most finitely many optimal subvarieties of defect at most $d$.

This conjecture is stated as an equivalent formulation of the atypical-intersection conjecture above. It was formulated by Habegger and Pila, building on the notion of defect introduced by Pink; the source does not specify a resolution in this generality.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every abelian variety and subvariety over algebraically closed K, each defect bound d, finitely many optimal subvarieties.
technical_assessment: Special-subvariety convention and field characteristic need body. This is a general unlikely-intersections finiteness problem, not bounded enumeration; no full arithmetic-geometric route.

title: The all-codimension stability conjecture for Hamming-cube subcubes
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional Hamming cube with vertex set $V$. For a set $A\subseteq V$, let $\mu(A)=|A|/2^n$, let $\nabla(A,B)$ denote the set of edges between $A$ and $B$, and let $\partial(a)$ be the minimum vertex boundary among sets of size $a$. Suppose $(A,B,W)$ is a partition of $V$. For $k\in\mathbb P$, the statement below refers to the conclusion that there is a codimension-$k$ subcube $C$ with $\mu(C\mathbin{\Delta}A)=O(\epsilon)$ under the hypotheses of Theorem 
$$
, with the theorem's corresponding edge and measure conditions.

**All-codimension stability conjecture.** The statement in Theorem
$$
 holds for all $k\in\mathbb P$, even with $n^\beta$ replaced by $2^n/\partial(|A|)$.

The conjecture extends the proved stability theorem from $k\in\{1,2\}$ to every positive codimension and replaces the stated control on the exceptional set by a quantity involving the minimum vertex boundary. The source gives no resolution of this extension.
quantifiers_and_scope: Purported all-positive-codimension extension of an unnamed theorem with changed exceptional-set control.
technical_assessment: Literal statement has missing theorem numbers, hypotheses and broken display. Cannot reconstruct edge/measure conditions or count it as a complete mathematical statement. No attempted proof.

title: Galois-orbit equidistribution conjecture for torsion points and Laurent polynomials
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $d\geq 1$, let $P\in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}[X_1^{\pm 1},\ldots,X_d^{\pm 1}]\setminus\{0\}$, and let $m(P)$ denote the logarithmic Mahler measure of $P$. For $\boldsymbol{\zeta}\in\mathbb{G}_m^d$ of finite order, let $\delta(\boldsymbol{\zeta})$ denote the minimum degree of a coordinate of $\boldsymbol{\zeta}$ over a proper algebraic subtorus, as defined in the paper. **Galois-orbit equidistribution conjecture.** For each $P$ there exists $\kappa>0$ such that, whenever $\delta(\boldsymbol{\zeta})$ is sufficiently large, one has $P(\boldsymbol{\zeta}^\sigma)\neq 0$ for every $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\boldsymbol{\zeta})/\mathbb{Q})$ and

$$
\frac{1}{[\mathbb{Q}(\boldsymbol{\zeta}):\mathbb{Q}]}\sum_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\boldsymbol{\zeta})/\mathbb{Q})}\log|P(\boldsymbol{\zeta}^\sigma)|=m(P)+O(\delta(\boldsymbol{\zeta})^{-\kappa})
$$

as $\delta(\boldsymbol{\zeta})\to\infty$, with the implicit constant depending only on $d$ and $P$. The conjecture extends the quantitative torsion-point estimate of Lind, Schmidt, and Verbitskiy from finite subgroups to individual Galois orbits. The case $d=1$ follows from work of Baker, Ih, and Rumely, while the stated two-dimensional example remains open.
quantifiers_and_scope: For each nonzero Laurent P in any dimension, some positive exponent uniformly over sufficiently independent torsion points.
technical_assessment: Delta is only paraphrased and may not be the paper's actual independence invariant. Nonvanishing plus quantitative log singularity control are required; one-dimensional Baker bounds do not give all dimensions. No clearance.

title: The measure partitioning conjecture for non-atomic measures on the circle
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $n\ge2$. Let $\mu_1,\mu_2,\dots,\mu_n$ be non-atomic probability measures on the unit circle $S^1$, and let $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\dots,\alpha_n$ be non-negative reals summing to $1$. A partition of the set $[n]$ is written $[n]=P\cup Q$, and a partition of the circle into two intervals is written $S^1=X\cup X^c$. **Measure partitioning conjecture.** There exists a partition $[n]=P\cup Q$ into two nonempty sets and a partition $S^1=X\cup X^c$ into two intervals such that

$$
\min_{i\in P}\mu_i(X)=\sum_{j\in P}\alpha_j
$$

and

$$
\min_{i\in Q}\mu_i(X^c)=\sum_{j\in Q}\alpha_j.
$$

If true, this conjecture would imply by a simple inductive argument that the minimum number of cuts needed for disproportionate division is $f(n)=2n-2$ for all $n\ge2$; the claim is motivated by the possibility of deeper topological considerations.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every n>=2, all nonatomic circle measures and nonnegative demand vectors; nonempty P,Q and complementary arcs satisfy two exact minima.
technical_assessment: Primary arXiv1909.07141v1 Conjecture3.1 agrees; n=2 explicitly known via Stromquist-Woodall and n=3 left unsettled there. Moving endpoints provides two variables but active-minimum sets can switch; intermediate-value argument alone fails to fix P,Q. No full topological route.

title: Positivity conjecture for the Jacobian of the multigraph moment map
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $h:\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{\mathbf{0}\}\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be defined componentwise by

$$
h_i(\boldsymbol{\beta})=\sum_{j\ne i}\frac{\beta_i\beta_j}{2\psi-\beta_i\beta_j}.
$$

Let $\mathbf{J}$ be the Jacobian of $h$, and let

$$
\mathcal{B}=\{\boldsymbol{\beta}\mid \boldsymbol{\beta}>\mathbf{0},\;\boldsymbol{\beta}\boldsymbol{\beta}^{T}>2\psi\mathbf{E}\}.
$$

For $\boldsymbol{\beta}\in\mathcal{B}$, let $\lambda_n(\boldsymbol{\beta})$ be the smallest eigenvalue of $\mathbf{J}(\boldsymbol{\beta})$. **Positivity conjecture.** For all $\boldsymbol{\beta}\in\mathcal{B}$, $\lambda_n(\boldsymbol{\beta})>0$. In particular, $\mathbf{J}$ is positive definite and nonsingular. Furthermore, if $\boldsymbol{\beta}\geq 1$ entrywise, then $\lambda_n(\boldsymbol{\beta})\geq 1$. Numerical evidence suggests this conjecture, which would establish nonsingularity and positive definiteness of the Jacobian on the feasible set.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every beta in displayed B, positivity and beta>=1 strengthening; psi is undefined in record.
technical_assessment: Primary arXiv1909.09037v2 instead defines 2psi=sum beta, physical well-behaved domain B_delta and proves Lemma15 for n>=5 with a smaller positive lower bound. AppendixB derivation/proof inspected. Literal greater-than domain and lambda_n ordering conflict with source conventions; no new counterexample or full-scope retirement claimed.

title: Structural conjecture for near-extremal $K_{r+1}$-free graphs
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $r\geq 2$ be an integer, let $n$ be sufficiently large, and let $D_r(G)$ denote the minimum number of edges that must be deleted from a graph $G$ to make it $r$-partite. For graphs $G$ and $H$, write $G\otimes H$ for their join, and let an unbalanced blow-up mean a blow-up whose vertex classes need not have equal sizes.

**Structural conjecture.** There exists $\alpha_0>0$ such that, for every $0\leq\alpha\leq\alpha_0$ and every $K_{r+1}$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, there is an unbalanced blow-up $H$ of $K_{r-2}\otimes C_5$ on $n$ vertices satisfying

$$
e(H)\geq e(G)
$$

and

$$
D_r(G)\leq D_r(H).
$$

The conjecture proposes that the worst examples for the distance from $r$-partiteness among near-extremal $K_{r+1}$-free graphs have the form of unbalanced $K_{r-2}\otimes C_5$ blow-ups. The supplied text does not state whether this structural statement has been resolved.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every r>=2, sufficiently large n, small alpha and every purported near-extremal K_(r+1)-free G.
technical_assessment: Alpha never occurs in any edge-density hypothesis in literal record. Missing near-extremal condition materially widens scope. An all-graphs counterexample would not answer intended near-extremal question; source repair needed.

title: Khot's Unique Games Conjecture in transversal-polynomial form
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $X^{\alpha}$ be an $r$-fold cover of a graph $X$, where $\xi(X^{\alpha},t)$ is the transversal polynomial and $\deg(\xi(X^{\alpha},t))$ is the maximum number of edges satisfied by a labelling of $X$. For all $\epsilon,\delta>0$, there exists $r=r(\epsilon,\delta)$ such that, given an $r$-fold cover $X^{\alpha}$ of a graph $X$, it is NP-hard to distinguish between the following two cases:

1. $\deg(\xi(X^{\alpha},t))\geq(1-\epsilon)|E(X)|$;
2. $\deg(\xi(X^{\alpha},t))\leq\delta|E(X)|$.

This is the Unique Games Conjecture, a central complexity-theoretic hypothesis whose truth would imply optimality results for approximation algorithms for several NP-hard problems. In this formulation, the degree of the transversal polynomial records the maximum number of edges satisfied by a labelling; the source provides no resolution of the conjecture.
quantifiers_and_scope: For all epsilon,delta>0 some r makes the two promise cases NP-hard to distinguish.
technical_assessment: Transversal polynomial, covers and promise conventions need primary definitions. This is UGC itself; rewriting the objective supplies no computational reduction or full proof. No bounded certificate route.

title: Linear Ramsey numbers and bounded co-chromatic number for finitely defined hereditary classes
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $X$ be a hereditary class of graphs, meaning that it is closed under taking induced subgraphs, and suppose that $X$ is finitely defined, meaning that it has finitely many minimal forbidden induced subgraphs. The **co-chromatic number** of a graph $G$ is the minimum number of subsets into which $V(G)$ can be partitioned, with each subset either a clique or an independent set. Ramsey numbers are **linear** in $X$ if there is a constant $k$ such that

$$
R_X(p,q)\leq k(p+q)
$$

for all natural numbers $p$ and $q$.

**Linear Ramsey–co-chromatic conjecture.** A finitely defined hereditary class is of linear Ramsey numbers if and only if it has bounded co-chromatic number.

Classes of bounded co-chromatic number are known to have linear Ramsey numbers, but the converse fails for general hereditary classes. The conjecture asserts that the two notions coincide among finitely defined classes.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every finitely defined hereditary class: uniform linear restricted Ramsey bound iff uniform bounded cochromatic number.
technical_assessment: Bounded cochromatic implies linear Ramsey by pigeonhole, hence that direction is routine. Converse must exploit finite forbidden list, not just finite examples; no general decomposition or obstruction route.

title: Arratia's divisibility conjecture for prime factors of a uniform random integer
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $N(n)$ be uniformly distributed on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, with prime factorization

$$
N(n)=\prod_{p\le n}p^{C_p(n)}.
$$

For each prime $p\le n$, let $Z_p$ be an independent geometric random variable with parameter $\frac{1}{p}$ and range $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, and define

$$
M(n)=\prod_{p\le n}p^{Z_p}.
$$

A **coupling** of $M(n)$ and $N(n)$ is a joint construction preserving their respective distributions. **Arratia's conjecture.** For all $n\ge 1$, it is possible to construct $N(n)$, $M(n)$, and a prime $P(n)$ such that

$$
N(n)\mid M(n)P(n)
$$

always. Equivalently, there exists a coupling such that

$$
\sum_{p\le n}\left(C_p(n)-Z_p\right)^+\le 1
$$

always. The conjecture proposes an especially strong coupling between the dependent prime-factor exponent process of a uniform random integer and its independent geometric limit process; the supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
quantifiers_and_scope: For every n a joint law preserves uniform integer and independent geometric prime exponents, with excess multiplicity<=1 almost surely.
technical_assessment: Geometric parameter convention needs clarification. Primewise marginal matching cannot ensure a single joint divisibility defect; a Hall/transport inequality over all upsets would be needed. Finite-n coupling tests alone cannot prove all n.

title: Talagrand's fractional expectation-threshold conjecture
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $X$ be a finite set and let ${\mathcal F}\subseteq 2^X$ be increasing. Let $p_c({\mathcal F})$ be the threshold defined by $\mu_p({\mathcal F})=1/2$. Define the fractional expectation-threshold $q_f({\mathcal F})$ as the largest $p$ for which there is a function $g:2^X\to\mathbb R^+$ satisfying

$$
\sum_{S\subseteq T}g(S)\geq1\quad\text{for every }T\in{\mathcal F},\qquad \sum_{S\subseteq X}g(S)p^{|S|}\leq\frac12.
$$

**Talagrand's fractional expectation-threshold conjecture.** There is a universal constant $K$ such that

$$
p_c({\mathcal F})\leq Kq_f({\mathcal F})\log|X|.
$$

This is a fractional relaxation of the Kahn–Kalai expectation-threshold conjecture. The source presents it as a conjecture of Talagrand and notes that a stronger theorem replacing $|X|$ by a smaller parameter is proved in the paper.
quantifiers_and_scope: Universal K for every finite increasing family with defined critical threshold, fractional cover bound times log ground-set size.
technical_assessment: Primary arXiv1910.13433v2 Theorem1.1 gives stronger log ell(F); definitions of weak p-small and q_f match record, and ell(F)<=|X| gives target in conventional nondegenerate/log conventions. Source identifies this as Talagrand relaxation. Proof reduction/Theorem1.6 concluding argument inspected, full dependency replay not done. Endpoint log(1) convention is a wording issue, not new discovery.

title: Stapledon's integrality conjecture for equivariant Ehrhart series
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $G$ be a finite group acting on a lattice polytope $P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$. Let $M$ be the sublattice obtained by translating the affine span of $P$ to the origin, and let $\rho:G\to GL(M)$ be the induced representation. For $g\in G$, let $P^g$ be the fixed-point polytope and let $M^g$ be the sublattice of $M$ fixed by $g$. Define $\operatorname{ind}(P)$ as the smallest positive integer $k$ such that the affine span of $kP$ contains a lattice point, and define $\det(I-\rho(g))_{(M^g)^\perp}$ using the restriction of $\rho(g)$ to $(M^g)^\perp$. **Stapledon's integrality conjecture.** For every $g\in G$,

$$
H^*[1](g)=\frac{\dim(P^g)!\cdot\operatorname{vol}(P^g)\cdot\det(I-\rho(g))_{(M^g)^\perp}}{\operatorname{ind}(P^g)}
$$

is a non-negative integer. This conjecture predicts an arithmetic integrality property of the evaluation of the equivariant Ehrhart series and is part of Stapledon's program; the supplied text does not give a general resolution.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every finite lattice-polytope action and every group element, normalized fixed-volume determinant/index expression integer.
technical_assessment: Volume lattice normalization, affine action and meaning of H*[1] require primary body. Arbitrary Euclidean volume would change claim. Rational fixed-polytope examples do not decide properly normalized integrality; no full route.

title: The surrogate maximum principle for tensor-product weights on n-trees
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $T^n$ be the $n$-tree, let $w:T^n\to[0,\infty)$ be a weight of tensor product form, and let $\mathbf{V}_{\delta}^{\mu}$, $\mathcal{E}_{\delta}[\mu]$, and $\mathcal{E}[\rho]$ denote the associated quantities. The **surrogate maximum principle** is the assertion that there are $\kappa>0$ and $C<\infty$ such that, for every pair of positive functions $\mu,\rho:T^n\to[0,\infty)$ and every $\delta>0$, 

$$
\int \mathbf{V}_{\delta}^{\mu}\,\mathrm{d}\rho\leq C(\delta|\rho|)^\kappa\bigl(\mathcal{E}_{\delta}[\mu]\mathcal{E}[\rho]\bigr)^{(1-\kappa)/2}.
$$

**Surrogate maximum principle.** Every such weight satisfies this principle with $\kappa=1/n$ and $C=C(n)$ independent of $w$. This is known for $n=1,2,3$; the conjecture concerns the general $n$-tree case and is used conditionally for the subsequent results.
quantifiers_and_scope: For every n and tensor-product weight, all positive mu,rho and delta, fixed exponent1/n and uniform C(n).
technical_assessment: Potentials, truncation and energies omitted. Reference calls refuted without witness identifying exact weight/domain; not enough to retire. Known n<=3 cases cannot tensorize through a general multiparameter truncation.

title: The Andr\e1sfai blow-up conjecture for triangle-free graphs
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $n$ and $s$ be integers with $n s\e 0$. For $k\e 2$, define

$$
g_k(n,s)=\tfrac12 k(k-1)n^2-k(3k-4)ns+\tfrac12(3k-4)(3k-1)s^2.
$$

Define $g(n,s)$ by

$$
g(n,s)=\begin{cases}
\frac12ns,&s\le \frac13n,\\
g_k(n,s),&\frac{k}{3k-1}n\le s<\frac{k-1}{3k-4}n\text{ for some }k\ge2,\\
\left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\right\rfloor,&\frac n2\le s\le n.
\end{cases}
$$

Here $\operatorname{ex}(n,s)$ denotes the maximum number of edges in a triangle-free $n$-vertex graph whose independence number is at most $s$. **Andr\e1sfai blow-up conjecture.** For all integers $n\ge s\ge0$, $\operatorname{ex}(n,s)\le g(n,s)$. Equivalently, every triangle-free $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)\le s$ has at most $g(n,s)$ edges. The conjecture is known for the ranges governed by $g_2$ and $g_3$, and is open only for $s\in(\frac13n,\frac38n)$. Its proposed bound is attained, for the most interesting range of $s/n$, by suitable blow-ups of Andr\e1sfai graphs.
quantifiers_and_scope: For all integers n>=s>=0, triangle-free graph edge maximum bounded by piecewise g(n,s).
technical_assessment: Corrupted inequalities in opening and undefined/infeasible edge regimes need care; intended hard interval is s/n between1/3 and3/8. Verifying Andrasfai blow-ups gives lower construction only, not upper extremal proof.

title: The Odd Alternating Cycle Conjecture
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field. For a directed graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, its minrank over $\mathbb{F}$, denoted by $\operatorname{minrk}_{\mathbb{F}}(G)$, is the minimum rank over $\mathbb{F}$ of a matrix representing $G$. An alternating odd cycle is a directed graph whose underlying undirected graph is an odd cycle and whose edge orientations alternate, with one exception.

**Odd Alternating Cycle Conjecture.** For every field $\mathbb{F}$ there exist $\varepsilon>0$ and an odd integer $\ell$ such that every $n$-vertex directed graph $G$ with

$$
\operatorname{minrk}_{\mathbb{F}}(G)\leq\varepsilon\cdot n
$$

contains an alternating cycle of length $\ell$.

The conjecture was proposed in connection with circuit-complexity questions and Valiant's approach to circuit lower bounds. It was disproved over the real field, while its status over finite fields remained open in the source context.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every field has some epsilon>0 and odd length ell forcing that alternating directed cycle in all sufficiently low-minrank graphs.
technical_assessment: Representing-matrix convention and containment need source. Record explicitly reports real-field disproof, which would defeat all-fields claim if body confirmed; finite-fields remainder is different scope. No body inspected, no confirmed retirement.

title: The quadratic-form conjecture for the $n-2$ Hessian equation
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $\bar\Gamma_k$ denote the Gårding cone for the $k$-th elementary symmetric polynomial $4\sigma_k\4$, and write $4\sigma_k^{jj}(kappa)=\partial \sigma_k/\partial \kappa_j4$ and $4\sigma_k^{ii,jj}(\kappa)=\partial^2\sigma_k/(\partial \kappa_i\partial \kappa_j)4$. Suppose that $kappa=(\kappa_1,\ldots,\kappa_n)\in\Gamma_k4$, $2k>n4$, $kappa_14$ is the maximum entry of $kappa4$, and for positive constants $N_04$ and $N4$ one has

$$
N_0\leqslant \sigma_k(\kappa)\leqslant N.
$$

For each index $1\leqslant i\leqslant n4$, if $kappa_i>\kappa_1-\sqrt{\kappa_1}/n4$, define

$$
a_j=\sigma_k^{jj}(\kappa)+(\kappa_i+\kappa_j)\sigma_k^{ii,jj}(\kappa).
$$

**The quadratic-form conjecture.** For every $n4$-dimensional vector $\xi=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n4$, the quadratic form

$$
\kappa_i\left[K\left(\sum_j\sigma_k^{jj}(\kappa)\xi_j\right)^2-\sigma_k^{pp,qq}(\kappa)\xi_p\xi_q\right]-\sigma_k^{ii}(\kappa)\xi_i^2+\sum_{j\ne i}a_j\xi_j^2
$$

is nonnegative when $kappa_14$ and the constant $K4$ are sufficiently large. Here $\sigma_k^{pp,qq}(\kappa)\xi_p\xi_q4$ denotes the repeated-index contraction of the second derivatives of $\sigma_k4$.

This conjecture is proposed as the key algebraic estimate needed for the global curvature estimate in the Hessian equation. The supplied passage gives no resolution or partial proof of the conjecture, so its status remains open.
quantifiers_and_scope: All admissible curvature vectors in Gamma_k, 2k>n, near-maximal i and all xi, eventually large kappa1,K.
technical_assessment: Repeated stray 4s and lost kappa macros obscure domain; threshold dependence on n,k,N0,N not explicit. Semidefinite checks at finitely many vectors cannot prove uniform Garding-cone inequality; no repaired statement or route.

title: The converse conjecture for the weak Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant and hollow polytopes
statement_exact_utf8:
A polytope $P\subset\mathbb Q^d$ is the convex hull of a finite set of points in $\mathbb Q^d$. A lattice $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Q^d$ is a discrete subset that is an affine image of $\mathbb Z^r$ for some $r\leqslant d$. For a point $q\in P$, let $\Gamma$ be the minimum face of $P$ containing $q$, and let $\Lambda$ be the minimum lattice containing all vertices of $\Gamma$. The point $q$ is an **integer point** of $P$ if $q\in\Lambda$. A polytope is **hollow** if its only integer points are its vertices, and $L(d)$ denotes the maximum number of vertices of a hollow polytope in $\mathbb Q^d$. Let $\mathfrak w(\mathbb F_p^d)$ denote the weak Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant of $\mathbb F_p^d$. **Converse conjecture.** For every $d\geqslant 1$ and all sufficiently large primes $p$, 
$$
\mathfrak w(\mathbb F_p^d)=L(d).
$$
 Proposition 1.3 gives the opposite inequality for every fixed $d$ and sufficiently large $p$, so this conjecture asserts that the lower bound obtained from hollow polytopes is sharp. The conjecture connects the extremal geometry of hollow polytopes with zero-sum phenomena in finite vector spaces; the provided text does not indicate whether it has been resolved.
quantifiers_and_scope: For every dimension, eventually every prime, weak EGZ constant equals maximum hollow-polytope vertex number.
technical_assessment: Weak EGZ constant is undefined in record and hollow is a source-specific face-lattice notion. Source lower bound is not upper bound. A converse compactness/structural classification uniformly in p is missing.

title: Li, Wu, Meng and Ma's $k$-tree connectivity conjecture for line graphs
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with at least $k$ vertices and at least $k$ edges, and let $L(G)$ be its line graph. For a set $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $|S|\geq 2$, let $\lambda_G(S)$ be the maximum number of edge-disjoint $S$-Steiner trees in $G$, and define $\lambda_k(G)$ as the minimum of $\lambda_G(S)$ over all $k$-subsets $S$ of $V(G)$. Similarly, let $\kappa_k(L(G))$ denote the minimum, over all $k$-subsets of $V(L(G))$, of the maximum number of internally disjoint Steiner trees joining that subset. **Li, Wu, Meng and Ma's conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 2$, if $G$ is connected and has at least $k$ vertices and at least $k$ edges, then

$$
\kappa_k(L(G))\geq \lambda_k(G).
$$

The conjecture would give a sharp relationship between generalized vertex-connectivity of a line graph and generalized edge-connectivity of the original graph. It is known for $k=2$, $k=3$, and $k=4$, while the general case is presented as an open conjecture.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every k>=2 and connected graph with enough vertices/edges: generalized vertex connectivity of line graph at least generalized edge connectivity.
technical_assessment: Terminal edges in G must become terminals in L(G) while preserving internally disjoint tree packing; merely taking line graphs of edge-disjoint Steiner trees can miss selected edges. Known k<=4 instances do not establish conversion for all k.

title: Optimality of a delta distribution for the lowest Dirac-Coulomb eigenvalue
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $D_0=-i\boldsymbol{\alpha}\cdot\nabla+\beta$ be the free Dirac operator, and let $\mu$ be a non-negative finite measure on $\mathbb{R}^3$ with Coulomb potential $V_\mu=\mu\ast|x|^{-1}$. Write $\lambda_1(D_0-V_\mu)$ for the lowest eigenvalue, and let $\lambda_1(\nu)$ denote the corresponding value when $\mu=\nu\delta_0$.

**Optimality for a delta.** The first eigenvalue is minimal when the charge distribution is concentrated at the origin, namely when $\mu=\mu(\mathbb{R}^3)\delta_0$. Equivalently, for all $0\leqslant\nu<1$,

$$
\lambda_1(\nu)=\lambda_1(D_0-\nu|x|^{-1})=\sqrt{1-\nu^2}.
$$

In particular, this would imply

$$
\nu_0=\nu_1=1.
$$

For the Schrödinger operator, the analogous delta-optimality statement is well known. The conjecture asks whether the same phenomenon holds for the Dirac operator and would determine the critical constants $\nu_0$ and $\nu_1$.
quantifiers_and_scope: All nonnegative Coulomb charge distributions of fixed mass<1 minimize first Dirac eigenvalue at a point.
technical_assessment: Displayed alleged equivalent equation is only explicit point-charge spectrum, already a special case, and omits universal distribution comparison. Operator realization and critical masses require body. No new outcome from recomputing Coulomb spectrum.

title: Planar basis evaluation conjecture for $eta_J$ on minimal kinematics
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $\Delta_{k,n}$ be the $k$th hypersimplex. For a $k$-element subset $J\subset\{1,\dots,n\}$, let $\Pi_J$ be the associated polytope obtained by eliminating the block containing $n$, and let $I_a$ and $I_b$ be the subsets constructed from the cyclic block decomposition of $J$, with $I_b=J\setminus S_{j-1}$ and $I_a$ the interval of length $k-s_{j-1}$ starting at the cyclically smallest element of $S_j$. Let $\eta_J$ be the corresponding planar basis element, let $x_i$ denote the minimal-kinematics variables, and call $J$ frozen when $\eta_J$ vanishes on minimal kinematics. **Planar basis evaluation conjecture.** For every nonfrozen $k$-element subset $J$ of $\{1,\dots,n\}$,

$$
\left.\eta_J\right|_{\mathrm{MK}}=\sum_{i\in I_a}x_i-\sum_{i\in I_b}x_i.
$$

Moreover, $I_a\setminus I_b$ and $I_b\setminus I_a$ are non-crossing; specifically, $i<j$ for every $i\in I_a\setminus I_b$ and $j\in I_b\setminus I_a$. For frozen $J$, one has $\left.\eta_J\right|_{\mathrm{MK}}=0$. The conjecture gives the proposed evaluation of planar basis elements on minimal kinematics; the supplied text does not state a resolution, so its status remains open.
quantifiers_and_scope: All nonfrozen k-subsets at every k,n give displayed minimal-kinematics linear form and noncrossing differences; frozen vanish.
technical_assessment: Eta_J, block construction, elimination and MK not defined enough to calculate. Cyclic indexing versus linear inequalities needs primary convention. A telescoping route is conceivable only after definitions and prior results are checked; no certificate claimed.

title: Frankl et al.'s conjecture on intersecting subfamilies of constrained set families
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $X=X_1\cup\cdots\cup X_p$ be a finite set partitioned into parts, let $k$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $a_1,\dots,a_p$ be integers satisfying $a_1+\cdots+a_p\leq k$ and $0\leq a_i<n_i$, where $n_i=|X_i|$. Define

$$
\mathscr{H}_3:=\left\{F\in\binom{X}{k}: |F\cap X_i|\geq a_i,\ i=1,\dots,p\right\}.
$$

**Frankl et al.'s conjecture.** If $n_i\geq2a_i$ for all $i$ and $n_i>k-\sum_{j=1}^pa_j+a_i$ for all but at most one $i\in[p]$ such that $a_i>0$, then the largest intersecting subfamily of $\mathscr{H}_3$ is trivial.

The conjecture identifies conditions under which an extremal intersecting subfamily must be trivial, meaning that all its members share a common element. The source presents this as a conjecture of Frankl et al.; no resolution is supplied in the paper or the provided context.
quantifiers_and_scope: All partitions and admissible k,a,n satisfying stated inequalities; largest intersecting family trivial.
technical_assessment: Existence of a trivial maximizer versus every maximizer trivial is ambiguous; tie cases can differ. Positivity and empty-family cases also need primary quantifiers. Product compression may be relevant but no extremal comparison proving all parameters established.

title: Dense induced subgraphs of large girth in bipartite graphs
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $t,k\in\mathbb{N}$. A bipartite graph has **average degree** at least $f(t,k)$ if its average degree is at least the value of a function $f:\mathbb{N}^2\to\mathbb{N}$; $K_{t,t}$ denotes the complete bipartite graph with $t$ vertices in each part, and an **induced subgraph** is obtained by taking a vertex subset together with all edges having both endpoints in it.

**The induced-subgraph conjecture.** There is a function $f:\mathbb{N}^2\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$ such that, for all $t,k\in\mathbb{N}$, every bipartite graph of average degree at least $f(t,k)$ has either a $K_{t,t}$-subgraph or an induced subgraph of average degree at least $t$ and girth at least $k$.

This strengthens Thomassen's conjecture by allowing an induced-subgraph conclusion, with $K_{t,t}$ as the stated obstruction. The paper proves the assertion when the graph has maximum degree at most a fixed multiple of its average degree, while the general conjecture remains open.
quantifiers_and_scope: For each t,k a finite threshold forces biclique or induced girth>=k subgraph with average degree>=t in every bipartite graph.
technical_assessment: Bounded maximum/average ratio is only a source partial case; removing high-degree vertices may remove required average degree. No uniform extraction mechanism survives arbitrary degree concentration.

title: Orbifold conjecture for twisted intertwining operators
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $V$ be a vertex operator algebra satisfying the following conditions: $V$ is simple, $V_{(0)}=\mathbb{C}\mathbf{1}$, $V_{(n)}=0$ for $n<0$, and the contragredient $V'$ is equivalent to $V$ as a $V$-module; $V$ is $C_{2}$-cofinite, meaning that $\dim V/C_{2}(V)<\infty$, where $C_{2}(V)$ is spanned by $\operatorname{Res}_{x}x^{-2}Y(u,x)v$ for $u,v\in V$; and every grading-restricted generalized $V$-module is completely reducible. Let $G$ be a finite group of automorphisms of $V$.

**Twisted intertwining-operator conjecture.** The twisted intertwining operators among the $g$-twisted $V$-modules, for all $g\in G$, satisfy associativity, commutativity and modular invariance.

This is presented as a main conjecture for orbifold conformal field theory and is intended to provide the structural properties needed to construct the orbifold theory. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence.
quantifiers_and_scope: For every VOA satisfying three rationality/cofiniteness conditions and finite automorphism group, twisted operators satisfy three structural properties.
technical_assessment: Associativity/commutativity/modular-invariance meaning and module categories need body. Reference solved quotation concerns rigidity of untwisted category and does not prove full orbifold claim. No retirement from that quotation.

title: The conjecture that all gapped fracton schemas are lax-topological
statement_exact_utf8:
A **lax-topological** $D$-dimensional Hamiltonian schema satisfies $TQO0$, $TQO1$, and $TQO2$, and there exist constants $\alpha$ and $\beta$ depending only on $D$ such that

$$
GSD(H_\Delta)\leq \alpha e^{\beta L^{D-2}}
$$

for every Hamiltonian $H_\Delta$ from the schema on a linear-size $L$ cellulation $\Delta$ of a space manifold $Y$. A gapped fracton schema is a Hamiltonian schema describing a gapped fracton phase. **The conjecture.** All gapped fracton schemas are lax-topological. This would place gapped fracton phases within the stated growth bound, extending the lax-topological framework beyond ordinary topological phases. The surrounding discussion notes that Haah codes saturate the bound, while it remains open whether intermediate maximum growth functions occur between TQFTs and Haah codes.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every gapped fracton schema, dimension-dependent constants controlling all cellulations plus TQO0/1/2.
technical_assessment: Schema, phase equivalence, TQO axioms and cellulation class absent. Tensoring decoupled lower-dimensional systems may change intended schema axioms; no legitimate full-scope counterexample without those definitions.

title: Characterization of cluster complexes by root independence and full support
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be the relevant Coxeter-system word set, and let $Q$ be a word in $\mathcal{S}$. For a spherical subword complex $\mathcal{SC}(Q)$, call it **root-independent** if, for every facet $I$, the multiset

$$
{{\sf R}}(I)=\big\{\!\big\{ {{\sf r}}(I,i)\mid i\in I\big\}\!\big\}
$$

is linearly independent, and call it **of full support** if every position of $Q$ belongs to some facet. A Coxeter element $c$ and a fixed reduced word $\mathrm{w_\circ}(c)$ determine the word $c\,\mathrm{w_\circ}(c)$.

**Cluster-complex characterization conjecture.** The following statements are equivalent: (i) up to commutations of consecutive commuting letters, $Q=c\,\mathrm{w_\circ}(c)$ for some Coxeter element $c$; (ii) $\mathcal{SC}(Q)$ is root-independent and of full support.

The conjecture proposes that these two properties characterize cluster complexes among spherical subword complexes. The supplied passage gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every spherical subword complex word: root-independent full support iff Coxeter sorting-word form up to commuting letters.
technical_assessment: Underlying finite Coxeter system, Demazure target and root function need primary definitions. Independence could require maximal rank/irreducibility conventions. Tiny reducible examples cannot be promoted before intended scope and closest bodies checked.

title: Erdős–Taylor conjecture on the supremum of planar random-walk local times
statement_exact_utf8:
For $x\in\mathbb{Z}^2$ and $N\geq 1$, let $\ell_x^N$ be the total number of visits to $x$ by a planar simple random walk started at the origin before exiting $[-N,N]^2$. Define the random Borel measure $\mu_N$ on $\mathbb{R}^2\times\mathbb{R}$ by

$$
\mu_N(A\times T)=\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^2}\mathbf{1}_{\{x/N\in A\}}\mathbf{1}_{\{\sqrt{\ell_x^N}-2\pi^{-1/2}\log N+\pi^{-1/2}\log\log N\in T\}}
$$

for Borel sets $A\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ and $T\subset\mathbb{R}$. Let $\mu$ be the critical Brownian multiplicative chaos in $[-1,1]^2$ with the origin as starting point. **Erdős–Taylor conjecture.** There exist constants $c_1,c_2>0$ such that $(\mu_N,N\geq1)$ converges in distribution, for the topology of vague convergence on $\mathbb{R}^2\times(\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\})$, towards

$$
\operatorname{PPP}(c_1\mu\otimes c_2e^{-c_2t}\,dt).
$$

In particular, for every $t\in\mathbb{R}$,

$$
\mathbb{P}\left(\sup_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^2}\sqrt{\ell_x^N}\leq\frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}}\log N-\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\log\log N+t\right)\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{}\mathbb{E}\left[\exp\left(-c_1\mu([-1,1]^2)e^{-c_2t}\right)\right].
$$

The conjecture concerns the extremal process and maximum of planar random-walk local times, whose logarithmic centering is predicted by the theory of extremes of log-correlated fields. The leading-order term $2\pi^{-1/2}\log N$ was conjectured by Erdős and Taylor and has been proved; the full extremal-process and limiting-law statement remains unresolved.
quantifiers_and_scope: Full centered planar walk local-time point process converges to a chaos-driven PPP, hence explicit maximum limit law.
technical_assessment: Literal record distinguishes proved leading order from unproved full extremal process while reference calls solved. A leading-order theorem does not imply centering/loglog or limiting law; neither retirement nor new proof claimed.

title: The geometric Langlands conjecture for irreducible local systems
statement_exact_utf8: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a smooth projective curve over $k$, and let $G$ be a reductive group over $k(X)$ with Langlands dual group $\LG$. Let $S\subset X$ be a finite set. For every irreducible $\LG$-local system $E$ on $X-S$, there exists a non-zero perverse sheaf $\sA=\sA_E$ on the moduli of $G$-bundles on $X$, equipped with appropriate level structure on $S$. **The geometric Langlands conjecture.** The perverse sheaf $\sA$ is a Hecke eigensheaf with eigenvalue $E$. This is a core conjecture of the geometric Langlands program, which seeks a duality between moduli of $\LG$-local systems on $X$ and moduli of $G$-bundles on $X$. The paper's abstract says that the authors construct the relevant Hecke eigensheaves for irreducible hypergeometric local systems, but the general statement above is not established here.
quantifiers_and_scope: For every irreducible dual-group local system on punctured curve exists nonzero level-structured perverse Hecke eigensheaf.
technical_assessment: Field characteristic, coefficients, local-system notion, reductive group and level structures need body. Hypergeometric case is a parameter subclass; deep general program cannot be promoted through abstract mention of a construction.

title: Rainbow tight Hamilton cycle conjecture for Dirac hypergraphs
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $k\geq 3$ and $\gamma>0$. A colored $k$-graph $(\mathcal{H},\phi)$ has minimum codegree $\delta_{k-1}(\mathcal{H})$, and for each color class $\mathcal{H}_i$ write $\Delta_0(\mathcal{H}_i)$ for its number of edges and $\Delta_{k-1}(\mathcal{H}_i)$ for its maximum codegree. A **properly colored tight Hamilton cycle** $C_n^{(k)}(k-1)$ is a tight Hamilton cycle whose intersecting edges receive distinct colors.

**Rainbow tight Hamilton cycle conjecture.** For every $k\geq 3$ and $\gamma>0$ there exist $c>0$ and $n_0>0$ such that if $(\mathcal{H},\phi)$ is an $n$-vertex colored $k$-graph with $n\geq n_0$, $\delta_{k-1}(\mathcal{H})\geq(1/2+\gamma)n$, $\Delta_0(\mathcal{H}_i)\leq cn^{k-1}$ and $\Delta_{k-1}(\mathcal{H}_i)\leq cn$ for every $i\in\mathbf{N}$, then $(\mathcal{H},\phi)$ contains a properly colored tight Hamilton cycle $C_n^{(k)}(k-1)$.

This is a proposed rainbow analogue of the paper's Dirac-type results for properly colored tight Hamilton cycles. The source presents it as a conjecture and does not provide evidence of a resolution.
quantifiers_and_scope: For all k>=3,gamma>0 some c,n0 forces tight Hamilton cycle under codegree and per-color size bounds.
technical_assessment: Title says rainbow while conclusion requires distinct colors only on intersecting edges. Reference cites graph-era resolutions unrelated to full hypergraph quantifiers. Properly colored versus rainbow scopes must be fixed from primary body; no retirement or claimed new construction.
